principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + Refactoring UI §1 Hierarchy (centered modals are the convention) + Jakob's Law
location: src/components/recipes/AttachRecipeModal.tsx line 155 — the native <dialog> element opened from RECIPE → [ + ] Attach recipe on /projects/[id]
screenshot: see audit narrative — measured bounds: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 480, height: 302 }
problem: The AttachRecipeModal native <dialog> opens pinned to the top-left corner of the viewport, not centered. ShareModal opens correctly centered. Measured DOM bounds at full-page state confirm the dialog renders at (0,0) — not the browser default centered-via-showModal() behavior. The user clicks 'Attach recipe' on a project's RECIPE card on the right-hand side of the screen, their eye is at ~1100px x-coord, and the modal appears 1000px away in the opposite corner. Saccade + confusion + 'did it open?' moment every time. The two modal patterns coexisting in the same product disagree about where modals live.
fix: In src/components/recipes/AttachRecipeModal.tsx line 155, add `m-auto inset-0` to the dialog className — copy the pattern from ShareModal.tsx line 190 verbatim. Final className should be `frame-strong p-0 bg-[var(--color-bg-panel)] text-[var(--color-fg)] backdrop:bg-black/70 m-auto inset-0 w-[480px] max-w-[92vw]`. One-line CSS class edit. Verify by reopening the modal — bounds.x should now be ≈847 on a 2174px viewport (centered for a 480px dialog).

principle: Design system token consistency + NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + the project's own design tokens (--status-wishlist: yellow)
location: src/components/wishlist/WishlistTable.tsx lines 29-33 — STATUS_PILL mapping
screenshot: wishlist populated row — STATUS pill renders 'WANTED →' in cyan, not yellow
problem: The design tokens explicitly define `--status-wishlist: var(--color-yellow)` and globals.css declares `.pill-wishlist { color: var(--status-wishlist); }`. The Round-3-implemented yellow wishlist semantic was supposed to apply across the app to indicate 'wanted but not yet bought'. But WishlistTable maps `Wanted: 'info'` (cyan), not `Wanted: 'wishlist'` (yellow). On the populated wishlist row, the STATUS pill therefore renders in cyan — same colour as the active filter chip, same colour as 'Attached · …' on recipes, same colour as the active nav rail item. The yellow semantic is built but not used on the surface most associated with wishlisting. The brief explicitly flagged this for verification — 'WishlistTable — the yellow Wanted semantic still consistent?' — the answer is no.
fix: Change STATUS_PILL in src/components/wishlist/WishlistTable.tsx line 30 from `Wanted: 'info'` to `Wanted: 'wishlist'`. Bought stays `'ok'` (green) since the owned-semantic is also green, Cancelled stays `'neutral'` (muted grey). One-line edit. After the change, the wishlist row, the wishlist tab in the nav, and any future shopping/inventory surface speak the same yellow language for 'wanted'.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of System Status + Doherty Threshold (system feedback under 400ms increases perceived responsiveness)
location: src/components/NewProjectForm.tsx (project create), src/components/recipes/NewRecipeButton.tsx (recipe create), src/components/wishlist/QuickAddBar.tsx (wishlist add)
screenshot: verified by clicking through Projects /new → submit → land on detail page; Recipes /create-first-recipe → land on editor; Wishlist quick-add → row appears in table
problem: Three of the most common user actions in the app fire silently. Creating a project: form submits, you're redirected to the project detail page, no toast. Creating a recipe from the empty state: clicking the CTA navigates to the editor with no confirmation. Adding a wishlist item via the quick-add bar: the row appears in the table with no toast and the input is cleared in place. Compare to InventoryControls which DOES fire `toast.success('Added to wishlist')` after toggling the star on a paint — that one feels alive, the others feel like the click might have missed. The ToastProvider, useToast() hook, and success styling all already exist (verified — adding a paint to wishlist fires a green 'ADDED TO WISHLIST' toast top-center). The infrastructure is there; three high-frequency mutations just aren't wired.
fix: In src/lib/actions/projects.ts createProject (or wherever the project-create server action resolves), import the toast hook and call `toast.success('Project created — ' + project.name)` after the redirect; same pattern for createRecipe and the wishlist quick-add. Since server actions can't directly call client hooks, either (a) attach the toast call in the form's onSubmit handler after `await action()` resolves with ok:true, or (b) read a one-shot toast intent from sessionStorage on the destination page. Pattern (a) is cleaner and already used by InventoryControls. Three function calls. Coverage matters more than wording; the user must know their action landed.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — interactive elements must be at least 24×24 CSS px
location: src/components/library/ViewModeToggle.tsx (LIST/GRID toggle), src/components/wishlist/WishlistFilters.tsx (Wanted/Bought/Cancelled/All + category filter chips), src/components/tools/wheel/HarmonyPicker.tsx (COMPLEMENTARY/ANALOGOUS/TRIADIC/TETRADIC/SPLIT-COMP./SQUARE/MONOCHROMATIC/ACCENTED ANALOGOUS), MatchClient brand filter chips
screenshot: measured DOM bounds for ViewModeToggle: 53.8×17.33 px; WishlistFilter chips: 19.8–46.2px × 16.5px; HarmonyPicker buttons: ~80×24px (just-passes-but-marginal); MatchClient brand chips: similar
problem: Multiple high-frequency interactive controls fail WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8's 24×24 px minimum target size. The LIST/GRID view toggle on /library measures 53.8×17.33 — short axis 17.33px = ~73% of the minimum. The wishlist status/category filter chips measure 16.5px tall. HarmonyPicker buttons clear 24px via `tap-target` padding but the visible glyph is 11px (`text-2xs`) so users on touchscreens routinely miss them. The app's own .tap-target rule guarantees min 32×32 on desktop / 44×44 on mobile — these components are not using it. On touch devices these are nearly impossible to hit accurately; on desktop they invite mis-clicks that switch view modes or filters unintentionally.
fix: Add `tap-target` class (already defined in globals.css line 474–483) to: ViewModeToggle button (currently `inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 px-3 py-1.5 …` — add `tap-target` to the className list); WishlistFilters chip buttons (FilterChip wrapper, both Status and Category rows); HarmonyPicker keeps `tap-target` but bump the font from `text-2xs` to `text-xs` (13px) so the visible glyph clears 12px — the WCAG sibling rule §1.4.4. For chips that visually need to stay small, set explicit `min-h-[32px]` and `min-w-[32px]` and centre the glyph. Three components, ~5 class-list edits total.

principle: Refactoring UI §1 Hierarchy (de-emphasise secondary text; use real tonal steps) + WCAG 2.2 §1.4.3 contrast paired with semantic intent
location: src/app/globals.css lines 28–34 — --color-fg / --color-fg-muted / --color-fg-subtle tokens
screenshot: globals.css source confirms the three tier values
problem: The text-hierarchy tokens have been lifted so high in Round 3 that they no longer encode hierarchy. Primary fg is #f5f5f5 (245). Muted is #f0f0f0 (240). Subtle is #d4d4d4 (212). Muted and primary differ by 5/255 — visually identical at any rendering size; the human eye cannot distinguish them on a dark backdrop. The comment in the file claims 'Some hierarchy preserved (subtle slightly dimmer than muted)' but muted is functionally identical to fg. The result: across the UI you cannot tell what's a label vs a value, what's metadata vs content, what's navigation vs body. Section labels (`SUB-PROJECTS · 0`, `ZONES · 1`, `RECIPE`, `SHOPPING FOR THIS`) all look the same weight as the actual content. Cognitive load goes up; scannability goes down. The previous round overshot the AA contrast fix.
fix: Re-establish the three-tier hierarchy. Drop --color-fg-muted to #c4c4c4 (196/255 — 10.5:1 against #0a0a0a, passes AAA) and --color-fg-subtle to #8e8e8e (142/255 — 5.4:1 against #0a0a0a, passes AA). That keeps all secondary text above AA while restoring a real visual gap: primary is ≈245, muted is 196 (Δ49), subtle is 142 (Δ54 from muted). Now the metadata reads as metadata. Section labels (`text-2xs uppercase tracking-wider text-[var(--color-fg-muted)]`) feel like chrome again, body text owns the surface. Two CSS variable edits.

principle: NN/g #5 Error prevention + WCAG 2.2 §3.3.4 Error Prevention (for legal/financial/data-loss actions) + Polaris destructive-action confirmation guidance
location: src/components/user/RecoveryEmailCard.tsx lines 66–77 + 117–124 — the Remove button on the verified recovery-email card
screenshot: /user page — the [ REMOVE ] button in the recovery email card
problem: The Remove button on the recovery email card fires `removeRecoveryEmail()` immediately on click with no confirmation step. Recovery email IS the user's password reset path (the entire UX-V3-002 finding existed because users without recovery email cannot reset). Removing it silently strips the user's only escape hatch from a forgotten password. The button is styled `variant='danger'` (red border) which signals risk but does not prevent it — a misclick is still terminal. The current toast-after-remove ('Recovery email removed.') is a confirmation of the action, not of the intent. WCAG 3.3.4 explicitly calls this kind of important-data deletion out as requiring confirmation, reversal, or check-and-confirm.
fix: Two acceptable patterns: (a) Confirm-then-act: clicking Remove changes the button into a two-step `Remove? [ Yes ] [ Cancel ]` inline confirmation that resolves on the second click. Cheaper than a modal, terminal-aesthetic-friendly. (b) Undo window: after Remove fires, show a sticky info toast for 8 seconds with an `[ Undo ]` action that re-adds the email. Pattern (a) is lower-effort and matches the rest of the app's text-button vocabulary. Add a confirmation state to the component (`const [confirming, setConfirming] = useState(false)`); first click sets it, second click fires onRemove. Reset on blur / 5-second timeout.

principle: NN/g #2 Match between system and the real world + NN/g #8 Aesthetic and minimalist design (don't promise what doesn't exist) + Information Scent
location: src/app/user/page.tsx lines 28–32 — the User page header subhead
screenshot: /user — `Profile · Sync · Inventory · Export · Preferences.` subhead with only two cards below
problem: The /user page header reads `Profile · Sync · Inventory · Export · Preferences.` — five comma-listed sections promised to the user. The page renders only TWO of them: Recovery email + Backup & export. The other three (Profile, Sync, Inventory, Preferences) do not exist. The user reads the subhead as a table of contents, scrolls expecting to find them, finds nothing, and concludes either the page is broken or they have somehow filtered to a subset. The User page is also where the brief expected /settings to live — currently /settings is a 404 — so a user looking for theme/accessibility/CRT-overlay preferences cannot find them either. The promise undersells what's there and oversells what isn't.
fix: Either (a) ship the missing modules first, or (b) trim the subhead to match what exists. Trim is the right call right now: replace line 30 with `Manage your recovery email and download a full backup of your data.` — describes only what's on the page, in plain language. When/if Sync/Inventory/Preferences modules ship, add them back to the subhead at that time. Bonus: rename the H1 from `USER` to `Account` — 'User' reads as 'the user' (you), 'Account' is the noun for the page contents. Two text edits.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + Material 3 brand chrome consistency + Jakob's Law (user-facing pages must feel like one product)
location: /api/auth/signout (NextAuth default page) — visible by visiting it directly or following the sign-out flow
screenshot: NextAuth default 'Signout' screen — pure black background, system font, no terminal aesthetic
problem: The sign-out confirmation page is the NextAuth library default — proportional system font, pure-black background, raw 'Signout' / 'Are you sure you want to sign out?' / 'Sign out' button. Zero connection to the Mini Manager terminal aesthetic: no glow-cyan H1, no `[ X ]` button styling, no mono font, no scanline overlay, no NavRail, no breadcrumb. The transition from the rest of the app to this page is jarring — it reads like a different product or a stale environment. After fixing UX-V3-001 (the auth funnel itself), this is the most visible brand inconsistency in the app.
fix: Either (a) replace the NextAuth default by adding a custom signOut page at src/app/sign-out/page.tsx with the project's frame-strong card, mono buttons, and the same chrome as sign-in/forgot — then set `pages: { signOut: '/sign-out' }` in src/auth.ts; or (b) skip the confirmation entirely and POST directly to /api/auth/signout from the NavRail user link with `csrfToken` — the user already clicked 'sign out', a confirmation is friction, not safety. Most modern apps go with (b). Either way it's one short page or one small auth-config edit. Don't ship the default chrome.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of System Status + Jakob's Law (Enter submits forms) + Hick's Law (don't add a button click when Enter would suffice)
location: src/components/recipes/ZoneList.tsx and src/components/wishlist/QuickAddBar.tsx — the inline add-zone input and the wishlist quick-add input
screenshot: verified by typing 'Carapace' in /recipes editor → pressing Enter → input retains value, no zone added; same for Wishlist /wishlist with 'Citadel Combat Patrol — Space Marines'
problem: Two prominent text inputs do not submit on Enter. In the recipe editor, typing a zone name and pressing Enter leaves the input filled and the count at ZONES · 0; you have to click the [ + ] Add button manually. In the wishlist quick-add bar, typing a title and pressing Enter does nothing; clicking the [ + ] suffix button is required. Every user expects Enter to submit a single-field form. The double interaction (type → reach for mouse → click) breaks flow for the painter who's mid-recipe and adding a list of zones. Compounded: the inputs do not visually communicate that Enter doesn't work, so the user repeatedly tries it and feels the app is broken.
fix: Wrap each input in a real `<form onSubmit>` (or attach onKeyDown for Enter) so pressing Enter triggers the same action as the [ + ] button. In src/components/recipes/ZoneList.tsx, the input that captures the new zone name should live inside a <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); onAdd(); }}>; same in QuickAddBar.tsx. Two small refactors. Keep the [ + ] button — discoverable button + keyboard shortcut, both win.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + Jakob's Law (× is universally close, ✗ is universally error/wrong) + Refactoring UI §3 Use colour and shape redundantly
location: src/components/library/InventoryControls.tsx lines 122 and 123 — the compact owned/not-owned toggle glyph
screenshot: compact OWN column in LibraryTable — shows ✗ glyph in fg-subtle for not-owned paints
problem: The compact OWN column toggle uses `✓` for owned and `✗` for not-owned. The `✗` heavy-X glyph is the same character we use as the close affordance throughout the app (`[ × ]` close button on PaintDetailPanel, ShareModal, AttachRecipeModal). Semantically `✗` reads as 'wrong / error / no / cancel'. A new user scanning the library sees a row of red-X-tinted glyphs and reasonably worries that something is wrong with each paint. The aria-label on the button says 'Mark as owned' but the visible glyph contradicts. Fitts is fine — the button is the right size — but the symbol is misleading.
fix: Replace the not-owned glyph with `☐` (an empty box, U+2610) or use the Lucide `Square` / `CheckSquare2` icons so the toggle reads as a checkbox: empty box → not owned, check-in-box → owned. The mental model — 'I am ticking off the paints I own from a catalog' — is now obvious. Change the two characters in InventoryControls.tsx compact branch. Owned and wishlist toggles can stay `★`/`☆` since the star metaphor is unambiguous.

principle: Refactoring UI §1 Hierarchy (large decorative type must earn its weight) + Aesthetic-Usability Effect (decoration that doesn't carry meaning erodes trust) + Information Scent
location: src/app/library/page.tsx + src/app/recipes/page.tsx + src/app/wishlist/page.tsx — the large background numeral '02' / '03' / '04' top-right of each surface
screenshot: captured on /library (02), /recipes (03), /wishlist (04) — the big faint numeral
problem: Library, Recipes, and Wishlist each render a large faint numeral in the top-right of the page: 02, 03, 04. Tools and Projects don't. There's no caption, no label, no explanation. A sharp visitor immediately reads them as data — 'is that the count of items? a paint number? a version number?' — and then realises they don't change, and then wonders why they exist. The most charitable read is they're ordinal page identifiers matching the navigation position (Projects=01 unrendered, Library=02, Recipes=03, Tools=04 missing, Wishlist=05 misnumbered). Either it's a charming terminal-OS chrome flourish or it's information without meaning. As-is it's neither — it sits in dead screen space and looks like a broken stat.
fix: Two acceptable directions: (a) Commit to the chrome — make the numerals consistent across all five primary pages (Projects=01, Library=02, Recipes=03, Tools=04, Wishlist=05) and explain them inline once, e.g. '03 // RECIPES // <description>' as the page header rather than as a free-floating glyph; treat them like terminal-shell pane IDs. (b) Remove them — they don't carry meaning right now and the empty space helps the existing decorative line under the H1 breathe. Direction (a) buys identity; direction (b) buys clarity. Pick one — what's there now is neither.

principle: NN/g #2 Match between system and the real world + Polaris empty-state guidance (status pills must read with the user's emotional context)
location: src/lib/projects/status.ts (and wherever the project EMPTY/PILE/BACKLOG status pill is computed) — the status pill on the project detail header
screenshot: captured on /projects/AbtFfHvn4C29kAGB — pill reads `EMPTY · 0%` on a brand-new project; on a project with one owned mini it reads `PILE · 0%`
problem: A user creates a project. They land on the detail page. The pill at the top right says `EMPTY · 0%` — a value-neutral statement of fact that lands as 'you have done nothing'. Project just born, already shamed. The status pill voice elsewhere in the app is warm and inviting (`No zones yet. Type your own with [ + ] Add zone or one-click populate a starter pack below.`). The single word `EMPTY` cancels that tone. The follow-up state `PILE` (when there are owned but unbuilt minis) is delightful and on-brand for miniature painters — 'pile of shame' is the community joke for unpainted minis. The new-project state needs the same care.
fix: Rename the EMPTY state to `READY` or `NEW` — communicates 'this is the starting line, not a failure'. Adjust src/lib/projects/status.ts (or wherever the status mapping lives) to map zero-counter projects to `READY · 0%` for greenfield projects and `PILE · X%` only once `ownedCount > 0 && buildCount === 0`. One label change, possibly a one-line conditional. The terminal-aesthetic deserves a status name that reads as `> BOOT_COMPLETE` not `> EMPTY`.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of System Status + aria-live error announcement + Doherty Threshold (stale error confuses recovery)
location: src/components/StageCounter.tsx — the inline error rendered after a failed cascade validation (visible after pressing `B` with owned=0)
screenshot: captured on /projects/AbtFfHvn4C29kAGB — pressed `B` with owned=0, then incremented owned to 1, error 'Build can't exceed Owned (0).' persists below the keyboard hint
problem:
Pressing a stage-shortcut against an invalid state produces a red inline message: `Build can't exceed Owned (0).` Good. But the error is rendered as a regular `

` with no `role='alert'` and no aria-live region — screen readers do not announce it. Worse, the error string captures the value at the moment it was raised, then never refreshes — after the user increments Owned to 1, the error still reads `Owned (0)`. The user has fixed the problem, but the message tells them they haven't. The error also has no dismiss button and no auto-clear, so it lingers below the keyboard hint indefinitely, jamming layout.
fix:
Wrap the error

in `role='alert'` (or use the existing `error` toast: `toast.error(result.error)` — InventoryControls already does this pattern). Clear the error state automatically whenever a counter changes (`useEffect(() => { if (counters.changed) setError(null); }, [counters.timestamp])`). If you keep the inline version, add a dismiss × and a 6-second auto-fade. Three lines: role='alert', useEffect clear, optional dismiss. Bonus: toast on validation failure so the screen-reader and visual-only users both get it.

principle: Refactoring UI §1 Hierarchy + NN/g #6 Recognition rather than recall (controls must read as controls) + Material 3 button affordances
location: many — `[ + ] New project`, `[ I ] Import army list`, `[ + ] Create your first recipe`, `[ + ] Add zone`, `[ + ] Add step`, `[ + ] ADD NAMED MODEL`, `[ + ] Attach recipe`, `[ SAVE PALETTE ]`, `[ SEND TO RECIPE ]`, `[ SHARE ]`, `[ DELETE ]`, `[ EXPORT ALL MY DATA ]`
screenshot: captured across /projects, /recipes, /wishlist, /tools/*
problem: Nearly every primary CTA in the app is rendered as bracketed text: `[ + ] Create your first recipe`. The bracket syntax is on-brand for the terminal aesthetic — it reads as a CLI option — but it eliminates the visual button affordance for users who haven't internalised the convention. A first-time visitor scans the page and sees what looks like plain text with a plus-in-brackets prefix; they don't always realise it's a clickable button. Compare to the input-pair Inventory stepper (`−` and `+` square frames with hover state and active feedback) — those read as buttons immediately. The DELETE button on the recipe header is especially risky: it's the same `[ DELETE ]` styling as the benign SHARE next to it, only red on hover; at rest both look like equivalent text links. The primary CTAs deserve real button styling (the .btn-primary / .btn-secondary tokens already exist).
fix: Promote the most important CTAs to real buttons. Use the existing .btn-primary class for the page-level primary action ([ + ] New project on /projects, [ + ] Create your first recipe on empty /recipes, [ + ] Add zone in editor empty state). Use .btn-secondary for adjacent actions (Import army list, Attach recipe). Keep the bracket syntax on tertiary controls and inside table rows where chrome density matters. For the recipe DELETE button: switch to .btn-danger so it's always-red, not hover-red — destructive actions must signal at rest. ~10 className edits across page templates + RecipeHeader.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + Material 3 tabs pattern (active state must be visually unambiguous)
location: src/components/recipes/AttachRecipeModal.tsx — TabButton component lines 323–345; same pattern in /library FilterRail brand accordion
screenshot: AttachRecipeModal element-screenshot — PICK EXISTING and CREATE NEW tabs sit side-by-side as text labels
problem: The Pick existing / Create new tab pair inside AttachRecipeModal lacks any visual tab affordance. Active gets `text-cyan + 10% cyan tint bg` and inactive gets default text-fg-muted — but there's no underline, no border, no separator line, no pill background. Side-by-side they read as two horizontal text labels, not as 'these are tabs and you can switch between two views'. The user has to click each to discover what they do. Same pattern recurs in the /library brand-letter accordion in the left filter rail where A, C, F, G, H, I, K, L, M, P, R all sit as single letters with a `+` suffix — no group label saying 'Brand · expand by initial' makes the column read as decoration. Tabs and accordions need affordance.
fix: For TabButton: when active, add a bottom-border accent: `border-b-2 border-[var(--color-accent)]`. Inactive gets `border-b-2 border-transparent`. That single visual element (active underline) is the universal tab convention. For the FilterRail accordion: add a section heading 'BRAND ·' above the letter list, and render each letter as a real disclosure (`<details><summary>A</summary>`) so the user sees a chevron and understands it opens. Two component-local edits.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (3:1 for non-text UI components) + colour-is-not-the-only-channel
location: src/components/library/LibraryGrid.tsx lines 116–128 — the 8×8 corner dots indicating owned (top-right) / wishlisted (bottom-right) on swatch cells
screenshot: /library grid view — yellow dots visible only at top-row positions on the dark-background swatches, invisible on cells with similar yellow tones; same problem with green dots on green swatches
problem: The owned (green) and wishlist (yellow) corner dots on the LibraryGrid swatch cells are 8×8 px (`h-2 w-2`) and rely entirely on hue contrast against the underlying swatch. A green-owned dot on a Goblin Green or Caliban Green swatch is invisible. A yellow-wishlist dot on Averland Sunset or Phalanx Yellow is invisible. The dots also overlap the same right edge of the cell (top-right vs bottom-right), so a paint that is BOTH owned and wishlisted shows two dots stacked on the same edge with no labels — the user can't read both states confidently at a glance. The 8×8 size is also at the edge of the WCAG 2.2 §1.4.11 3:1 non-text contrast requirement; against an arbitrary swatch the ratio routinely falls below 2:1.
fix: (a) Add a 1px outer ring with `border-2 border-[var(--color-bg)]` (already there) plus a contrasting 1px inner ring: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-fg)`. That gives the dot a visible boundary on any backdrop. (b) Bump the dot from h-2 w-2 (8px) to h-2.5 w-2.5 (10px) so the silhouette is more readable. (c) Move the wishlist marker from bottom-right to top-LEFT so owned and wishlist are on opposite corners — no stacking, instant scan. (d) Add the dual-state combination to the aria-label: `aria-label='${paint.name} — ${paint.brand} ${paint.hex} (owned, wishlisted)'`. Three CSS edits + one aria-label update.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of System Status — stubbed status that lies
location: src/components/StatusBar.tsx line 172 — the SAVED · IDLE segment
screenshot: top-of-viewport status bar on every authenticated desktop page
problem: The desktop StatusBar shows four segments: SYS · OK / NET · ON / SAVED · IDLE / TIME · 12:00:00. The SAVED · IDLE segment is hard-coded to 'IDLE' regardless of any actual save state. The source comment says 'SAVED is stubbed to IDLE — future: wire to a global dirty-state store'. The word 'IDLE' next to 'SAVED' actively misleads — it implies the save system is dormant when in fact the user just made changes that the optimistic-update toasts elsewhere confirm landed. A user who notices the bar reads it as 'oh, nothing's been saved'. Either the segment should reflect real state ('SAVED · 2s ago', 'SAVED · …', 'SAVED · DIRTY') or it shouldn't exist yet.
fix: Remove the SAVED segment from StatusBar until the dirty-state store is wired. Drop the segment + its Divider; the bar still has SYS / NET / TIME — three is plenty of chrome. When you ship the global dirty-state store, re-add SAVED with the real status. As a fallback if you'd rather keep the slot: change the placeholder from `IDLE` to `READY` (matches the proposed READY rename in UX-V4-012) — at least it reads as healthy rather than asleep.

principle: Doherty Threshold (perceived performance) + Aesthetic-Usability Effect (slow pages erode trust) + DOM size and content-visibility tradeoffs
location: src/components/library/LibraryGrid.tsx — renders all paints in a single grid container with content-visibility: auto
screenshot: /library grid view — measured domSize jumped from ~1.97MB (list view, 7144 paints) to ~5.79MB (grid view, same 7144 paints)
problem: Switching from LIST to GRID on /library balloons the DOM from ~1.97MB to ~5.79MB — a 3x jump. The grid renders all 7144 paints as separate <button> elements inside a single grid container, with content-visibility:auto on each cell for paint+layout skipping. The browser is still building the full DOM tree, attaching listeners, computing tooltip strings, allocating React fibers per cell. On a fresh desktop the switch is sluggish; on mobile it's noticeably worse. Scrolling through the grid is fine (content-visibility delivers), but the initial render of GRID after clicking the toggle has a perceptible 300–600ms lag. The list view caps the table to viewport-rendered rows via virtualization (apparent from the smaller DOM); the grid does not.
fix: Virtualize the grid the same way the list is. With ~50–80px swatches at 1440px viewport you fit ~16 columns × ~7 visible rows = ~112 cells onscreen. react-window's FixedSizeGrid is one drop-in option; alternatively keep the auto-fill grid template but bucket rows of 20 paints into outer <div> rows with content-visibility: auto and contain-intrinsic-size — the browser then skips the row-level layout for offscreen buckets. Goal: never have more than ~500 swatches in the live DOM at once. Should bring the GRID-mode domSize back below 2MB.

principle: Refactoring UI §7 Shadows and Depth (low-luminance content needs a visible boundary) + WCAG 2.2 §1.4.11
location: src/components/tools/gradient/RampDisplay.tsx — the ramp swatch cells in the right-side panel of /tools/gradient
screenshot: /tools/gradient — first ramp cell `#072547` (dark navy) is nearly invisible against the #0a0a0a app background
problem: The gradient ramp cells inherit no visible border. When the shadow input is a dark colour (e.g. #072547 — Prussian Blue Light), the resulting first ramp swatch is functionally indistinguishable from the surrounding #0a0a0a background. The user can read the hex code below it but can't see the swatch. The Tools/Wheel SwatchCard adds a `frame` border to swatches — RampDisplay doesn't. Consistency drift across the tools.
fix: Add `border border-[var(--color-border-strong)]` to each ramp cell in RampDisplay (or whatever the cell-wrapper className is). Now every cell has at least a 1px boundary regardless of fill colour. Same fix applies to the small swatch in the wheel-tool 'Active: #F20D0D' preview and any other naked swatch in the codebase. Three class additions.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + Refactoring UI §1 Hierarchy (anchor-actions belong where attention already is)
location: src/components/tools/ToolFooterActions.tsx — the floating bottom-right `[ SAVE PALETTE ]` `[ SEND TO RECIPE ]` row on all four tool pages
screenshot: /tools/wheel + /tools/eyedropper + /tools/match + /tools/gradient — bottom-right of viewport
problem: The two tool actions live in the bottom-right corner pinned to the viewport. On /tools/eyedropper with an empty palette, the SAVE PALETTE button is still enabled — clicking saves an empty palette. Not destructive but unhelpful. More importantly, the corner placement means: (1) on tall content pages the actions float above content, obscuring data; (2) the actions are far from the data they act on — the wheel sits top-left, the actions sit 1500+px away bottom-right (Fitts's Law); (3) on mobile (where the BottomTabBar already occupies bottom-edge real estate), the actions would either collide with the tab bar or get pushed up to a strange middle position.
fix: Disable SAVE PALETTE when the palette is empty (`disabled={paletteCount === 0}`). Move the actions to the right column header next to the SWATCHES · N count — that's where the data they act on lives, that's where Fitts wants them. On mobile, render them inline below the swatch list with a sticky-on-scroll behavior rather than fixed-bottom. One conditional + one layout move per tool page (or a shared container update if they share a wrapper).

principle: NN/g #6 Recognition rather than recall + Refactoring UI §3 Use real content (don't promise harmonies that don't exist)
location: src/components/library/PaintDetailPanel.tsx lines 207–219 — buildHarmonies() rotates the hue by 45° for any input paint
screenshot: /library?paint=15135 (AK Interactive 507b Admirality Medium Grey, #585E5A) — Harmonies row renders eight nearly identical grey cells
problem: The Harmonies row in the Paint Detail panel rotates the hue 45° eight times. For high-saturation paints (Mephiston Red, Lothern Blue) this produces a beautiful spread. For low-saturation paints (any grey, neutral khaki, off-white, off-black), all eight rotations land at essentially the same colour — saturation near zero means hue rotation produces a near-imperceptible visual difference. For the entire 'grey' and 'neutral' subset of the catalog (a large fraction of any miniature painter's library), the Harmonies row is empty information — eight cells the same colour. The user reads it as 'broken' or 'no harmonies available'.
fix: Either (a) when input HSL saturation is below a threshold (e.g. 0.15), boost the rotated outputs' saturation to a fixed value (e.g. 0.5) so the eight harmonies show as illustrative complementary hues at the input's lightness — they're no longer 'this paint's harmonies' but 'palette suggestions to pair with this neutral'. Update the section title to 'Pair with' when in that branch. Or (b) hide the Harmonies section entirely when the input is near-grey (saturation < 0.10) — replace with a single-line 'Neutral — no hue harmonies' caption. Option (a) is more useful; option (b) is more honest. Either is a small change in buildHarmonies + the section render.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + Refactoring UI Hierarchy
location: src/components/BottomTabBar.tsx — the mobile bottom nav contains 5 tabs (Projects/Library/Recipes/Tools/Wishlist); NavRail contains 6 (those + User)
screenshot: code-level — BottomTabBar.tsx lines 22–28 vs NavRail.tsx lines 26–35
problem: The mobile bottom tab bar exposes 5 destinations; the desktop nav rail exposes 6. The missing one on mobile is User. Mobile users CAN reach /user via the avatar in MobileHeader top-right, but that mental model differs from the BottomTabBar pattern — and on a mobile that uses the bottom bar as the primary nav (which is the iOS/Android convention), the User destination is invisible. A mobile user looking for User has to learn 'oh, that's up in the corner, not in the bar with everything else'. Inconsistency between primary nav widgets.
fix: Either (a) add User as a sixth BottomTab — five fits comfortably, six is still within Miller's-Law range and tabbars-at-6 are common (Reddit, X mobile); width math: 375px / 6 ≈ 62px per tab, still above the 44px touch target. Or (b) remove the User avatar from MobileHeader and route mobile users through the User tab only. Pick one path; consolidate. (a) gives every primary destination the same surface across viewports.
